subject.title: [Feature]: Add TTL/Expiry for Delivery Queue Messages

question: Which outbound delivery expiry contract should OpenClaw expose for stale queued messages: an opt-in messages.delivery-style config that preserves current default replay behavior, a new default TTL that expires stale entries automatically, or no core TTL for now?
rationale: The code fix is clear, but the product contract is not: default expiry can drop delayed legitimate recovery messages, while opt-in config adds a new public config surface that AGENTS.md says should have a high bar.

options.title: Opt-in expiry config
options.body: Add a strict, documented messages.delivery-style TTL and expire action while preserving current replay behavior by default for upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Default bounded expiry
options.body: Ship a conservative default TTL and migration/docs proof, accepting that some existing delayed-recovery setups will stop replaying old queued replies.

options.title: Do not add core TTL now
options.body: Keep recovery unchanged and close or defer stale-replay mitigation to operator cleanup or a broader lifecycle redesign.

recommendation.title: Opt-in expiry config
recommendation.body: Add a strict, documented messages.delivery-style TTL and expire action while preserving current replay behavior by default for upgrade compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the latest maintainer-facing direction on this issue and has strong recent history in the delivery queue files.
